<thought>From the spectrum, a clear M+2 peak at ~33 % of the base peak matches the characteristic 3:1 intensity ratio of a single chlorine atom (35Cl/37Cl). The noticeable M+1 peak (~10 % of the base) aligns with the natural 13C abundance, indicating carbon is present. No 1:1 M+2 pattern (bromine) or other distinctive isotopic patterns are evident. Therefore, the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
